newsitem.title: UK: UK INTEREST RATES ON HOLD FOR TIME BEING-ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: UK INTEREST RATES ON HOLD FOR TIME BEING-ANALYSTS.

text.p: British interest rates look set to stay on hold for the time being after the Bank of England said Thursday's quarter point rise was enough to ensure inflation will meet the government's target.
"The message is clear that that's it for now and it is highly unlikely rates will go up again in September," said Ian Stewart, UK economist at Merrill Lynch.
But he said the pace of economic growth and strong domestic demand in particular meant interest rates were far from reaching their peak and the Bank would have to tighten policy later in the year.
"Given the strength of the domestic economy, another rise later in the autumn is still on the cards."
The Bank of England raised rates by a quarter point to 7.0 percent on Thursday, the fourth rise in as many months.
However, in an unusually forthright statement, the central bank said the level of interest rates was now consistent with the 2.5 percent inflation target.
"Upward pressure on the exchange rate should be reduced by the perception that interest rates have reached a level consistent with the inflation target," the Bank said.

In its statement, the Bank said it was aware the high exchange rate has put pressure on firms who need to sell their goods abroad, but said the pound's upward march was due in large part to facts beyond its control.
Stewart said the shift in consensus thinking in the last two weeks or so away from further tightening may have prompted the Bank's statement.
"Although there was a good case for tightening policy, the consensus has grown more cautious about further rises and especially its effect on export growth," he said.
"The Bank is in the process of building credibility and was anxious to show it is alive to the problems faced by exporters."
But Michael Dicks, UK economist at Lehman Brothers, said while it was surprising the Bank made its comments today and did not wait for next week's inflation report, the statement was worded shrewdly.

"The wording of the statement is typical Bank of England. It was careful not to say enough has been done, only concede that the market has recognised that interest rates have reached the sort of level consistent with inflation hitting the target."
He said the Bank was signalling it would now be moving much more slowly, and the consensus was right to think economic growth would slow soon and price pressure abate.
"But the risk is still that enough has not been done." He forecast rates peaking near 8.0 percent.
Economists said next week's inflation report would flesh out the Bank's statement.

"It will suggest that the monetary tightening we have had over the last four months, combined with the strength of sterling, have increased the chances of meeting the inflation target," said Andrew Cates, UK economist at UBS.

The pound dropped by just over one pfennig on the Bank's statement to 3.0020/30 marks from 3.0130/40 before the news. It has appreciated by around 25 percent on a trade-weighed basis since last August.
And Cates forecasts that with some survey evidence already suggesting economic growth is slowing, little further action on interest rates is necessary.
"Although subject to some upside risk, we believe that we have reached the peak for base rates in the current interest rate cycle."
